mechanism_narrative: A current level of industrial production below 105 (relative to 2017=100) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO is below 105, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 3.6% in the most recent month signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises above 3.6%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a severe economic contraction, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction effect (measured by the coefficient in a regression) is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weak consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and RSAFS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1500 thousand units signals a collapsing housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 1500, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or the interaction effect (measured by the coefficient in a regression) is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.0%), a decline in employment (PAYEMS) signals an impending labor market slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.05.
